I had a customer come to the register to return some ink cartridges. Our return policy for ink is pretty strict, stating that we'll only refund ink if they (a) have the original receipt, (b) have the ink in its original, unopened package, and (c) return it within thirty days. Our store receives no compensation for returned ink sent back to the manufacturer, so it's understandable why it's strict. Here's how the interaction unfolded1:

Livunda Arock: I need to do an exchange.

Me: Alright, let me take a look.

LA revealed a plastic shopping bag and started to empty it. On the counter, he placed a sandwich bag of two raw ink cartridges, their respective empty packages, his receipt, and two of the same ink packages from our shelves.

Me: What's wrong with them?

LA: They don't work.

Me: Are you sure you have the right models for your printer?

LA: Yeah. They're the same numbers.

I didn't want to make the interaction malnourished too early on, so I gave him the benefit of the doubt.

Me: Since the packages are open, policy says I can't take this return, but I'll let it slide today.

Usually, reasonable customers become apologetic at this point and appreciate the leniency.

LA: But that doesn't sound fair. I'll only know if they'll work when I take them out.

Me: The odds of the cartridge faulting is pretty low, especially when you have two different ones. But the policy's there because of return scams, where a customer buys an ink cartridge, then takes an empty one back to the store and get a full refund. I'm not saying that's what's happening here, but that's why we're so strict.

As I was explaining, we were also going through the transaction process.

LA: But I never heard of that.

Me: Okay.

LA pulled out a coupon.

LA: Can I use this to lower the price of the new cartridges?

I scan the coupon and it doesn't register. My immediate thought was that it expired. I looked at the valid dates and confirmed.

Me: This coupon's expired.

LA: But other stores let me use it sometimes...

Me: Not here.

We finished the transaction as he took the coupon and put it back in his wallet.

Me: (Are you really going to take that expired coupon everywhere until you can use it?)

Looking back, I think I should've just denied the exchange request in the first place, since it was against policy and our company reserves the right to deny a return for any reason. Plus, my favorite manager was on duty. But, meh. I still find that coupon denial a small victory.

TL;DR: Customer wanted to return open ink cartridges. I told him about our policy about avoiding return scams and he was puzzled. Did not accept his coupon.
